newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-DALY STARTS WITH LEAD EARLY IN SECOND ROUND OF PGA.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-DALY STARTS WITH LEAD EARLY IN SECOND ROUND OF PGA.

text.p: John Daly teed off as the sole leader on Friday as firmer conditions at Winged Foot kept the early starters from overtaking his four-under-par standing in the second round of the PGA Championship.
Daly, a recovering alcoholic hoping to make it completely through his first major championship of the season, thrilled the huge galleries with a record-tying 66 on Wednesday.

Daly shared the overnight lead with Davis Love, who also took advantage of the layout softened by rain Wednesday, but Love dropped back to three-under par in a roller coaster ride through the front nine.
Teeing off later in the day was the dream threesome of Masters champion Tiger Woods (even par), U.S. Open winner Ernie Els (even) and British Open champion Justin Leonard (two under).
The new-look Daly, sporting a trim figure thanks to a new diet and exercise regimen, excited players and fans alike by exhibiting his explosive game Wednesday in his return to the championship stage.

Daly missed the Masters and British Open after undergoing treatment for his alcoholism and walked off the course in the middle of the second round at the U.S. Open in June with a bad case of the shakes.
Sharing the first-round lead here with Daly was Davis Love, who also shot a opening 66.

Love bogeyed the first and the third holes before bouncing back with birdies at five and six. The 33-year-old Love, fighting for a Ryder Cup berth as well as taking aim at his first major title, then bogeyed the eighth hole to stand at three under.
Also at three under par was 27-year-old Shigeki Maruyama of Japan, who improved by a stroke as he posted three birdies against two bogeys through his first 11 holes.

Jeff Maggert joined the rarified air of four under par himself for a brief time when he made his fourth birdie of the day at the 14th hole. But Maggert, who contended until the final few holes at the U.S. Open, bogeyed the next two holes to drop back.
Greg Norman, who lost in an 18-hole playoff here to Fuzzy Zoeller at the 1984 U.S. Open, took his score up to three under when he birdied the eighth hole but he slid back with a bogey at the next.
In the clubhouse at two-under-par 138 was Italian Costantino Rocca, who closed with two birdies to post his second successive 69.

Australian Robert Allenby, who began the day one shot behind co-leaders Daly and Love, slipped off the leaderboard after taking a double-bogey at the second hole, a bogey at the third and another bogey at the sixth.
